title: SpIDER: Spatially Informed Dense Embedding Retrieval for Software Issue Localization
abstract: arXiv:2512.16956v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Retrieving code functions, classes or files relevant to a user query, bug report or feature request from large codebases is a fundamental challenge for Large Language Model (LLM)-based coding agents. Agentic approaches typically employ sparse methods like BM25 or dense embedding strategies to identify semantically relevant units. While dense embedding approaches can outperform BM25 by large margins, both ignore the graph-structured characteristics of the codebase. To address this, we propose SpIDER (Spatially Informed Dense Embedding Retrieval), a dense retrieval approach that integrates LLM-based reasoning with graph-based exploration of the codebase. We further introduce SpIDER-Bench, a graph-structured benchmark curated from SWEPolyBench, SWEBench-Verified and Multi-SWE-bench, spanning Python, Java, JavaScript and TypeScript repositories. translated_title: SpIDER：面向软件问题定位的空间感知密集嵌入检索
translated_abstract: 从大型代码库中检索与用户查询、错误报告或功能请求相关的代码函数、类或文件，是基于大语言模型（LLM）的编程智能体面临的一项根本性挑战。智能体化方法通常采用BM25等稀疏方法或密集嵌入策略来识别语义相关的代码单元。虽然密集嵌入方法可以大幅超越BM25，但两者都忽略了代码库的图结构特性。为解决这一问题，我们提出了SpIDER（Spatially Informed Dense Embedding Retrieval，空间感知密集嵌入检索），这是一种将基于LLM的推理与代码库图结构探索相结合的密集检索方法。我们进一步推出了SpIDER-Bench，这是一个从SWEPolyBench、SWEBench-Verified和Multi-SWE-bench中精选构建的图结构基准，涵盖Python、Java、JavaScript和TypeScript仓库。SpIDER的基于图的候选扩展机制为候选单元的纳入提供了结构性依据……
tldr: 该论文提出SpIDER，一种将LLM推理与代码库图结构探索相结合的密集检索方法，用于软件问题定位，并发布了涵盖Python、Java、JavaScript和TypeScript四种语言的图结构基准SpIDER-Bench。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes SpIDER, a dense retrieval approach that integrates LLM-based reasoning with graph-based exploration of codebases for software issue localization, and introduces SpIDER-Bench, a graph-structured benchmark spanning Python, Java, JavaScript, and TypeScript repositories.
